question.problem:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $X∼N(3,{\sigma }^{2})$ is a normal random variable with $P(-1<X<7)=0.5346,$ find  $\sigma ,$ rounded to $2$ decimal places.

| $z$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,0.5\,$ | $\,0.6950\,$ | $\,0.6985\,$ | $\,0.7019\,$ |
| $\,0.6\,$ | $\,0.7291\,$ | $\,0.7324\,$ | $\,0.7357\,$ |
| $\,0.7\,$ | $\,0.7611\,$ | $\,0.7642\,$ | $\,0.7673\,$ |

*Hint: Note that the interval $-1<X<7$ is symmetric about the mean $\mu =3.$*
question.worked_solution:
First, note that the given interval is symmetric about the mean:

$$
P(-1<X<7)=P(3-4<X<3+4)
$$

So, we find the cumulative probability using symmetry:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-1<X<7) & =0.5346 \\ 2P(3<X<7) & =0.5346 \\ P(3<X<7) & =0.2673 \\ P(X<7)-P(X<3) & =0.2673 \\ P(X<7)-0.5 & =0.2673 \\ P(X<7) & =0.7673 \\ P(X\le 7) & =0.7673\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 7) & =0.7673 \\ P(Z\le \frac{7-3}{\sigma }) & =0.7673 \\ Φ(\frac{4}{\sigma }) & =0.7673 \\ \frac{4}{\sigma } & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.7673)\end{aligned}
$$

According to the table, we have

$$
Φ(0.73)=0.7673\,⇒\,{Φ}^{-1}(0.7673)=0.73.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{\sigma } & =0.73 \\ \sigma  & =\frac{4}{0.73} \\ \sigma  & ≈5.479\,45 \\ \sigma  & ≈5.48.\end{aligned}
$$
